subject: general
question: Which of the following Indian banks increased the minimum balance requirement for new customers for the semi-urban segment branches to ₹25,000, compared to its earlier ₹5,000 levels from August 1, 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**ICICI Bank**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **ICICI Bank**, one of India's leading private sector lenders, has implemented a substantial revision in its **minimum balance requirements** for specific branch categories.
 
• For **new customers** opening accounts in **semi-urban** segment branches, the **Average Monthly Balance (AMB)** requirement has been increased to **₹25,000**.
 
• This marks a significant jump from the earlier requirement of **₹5,000**, representing a five-fold increase in the threshold for **semi-urban** areas.
 
• The revised policy is set to come into effect starting from **August 1, 2025**. ***Hence, the correct answer is ICICI Bank.***
 
• Such adjustments are often made by private banks to align with their **operational costs** and to target specific **customer segments** that maintain higher liquidity in their accounts.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **ICICI Bank (Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India):**
 
 
• It is a prominent **Indian multinational bank** and financial services company headquartered in **Mumbai**, **Maharashtra**.
 
• The bank was originally promoted in **1955** by the **World Bank**, the Government of India, and representatives of Indian industry.
 
• The current **Managing Director** and **CEO** of the bank is **Sandeep Bakhshi**.
 
• It offers a wide range of banking products and financial services to corporate and retail customers through a variety of delivery channels and specialized subsidiaries.
 
 
 
• **Branch Classification in India:**
 
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** classifies bank branches based on population. **Semi-urban** branches are typically located in centers with a population of **10,000 to less than 1,00,000**.
 
• **Rural** centers have a population up to **9,999**, while **Urban** centers range from **1,00,000 to 9,99,999**, and **Metropolitan** centers have **10,00,000** and above.
 
 
 
• **Average Monthly Balance (AMB):**
 
 
• **AMB** is the minimum average balance a customer is required to maintain in their savings account over a month to avoid **non-maintenance charges**.
 
• It is calculated by adding the **closing balance** of each day in the month and dividing the total by the **number of days** in that month.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Comparison with Public Sector Banks:**
 
 
• In contrast to private players like **ICICI Bank** or **HDFC Bank**, public sector banks like the **State Bank of India (SBI)** have largely moved away from **AMB** penalties.
 
• **SBI** waived the **Average Monthly Balance** requirement for all **Savings Bank Accounts** in **March 2020** to encourage **financial inclusion** and provide relief to its vast customer base.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Customers:**
 
 
• High **minimum balance** requirements can act as a barrier for low-income individuals in **semi-urban** areas, potentially shifting them toward **Public Sector Banks** or **Small Finance Banks**.
 
• Failure to maintain the required **₹25,000** after the **August 1, 2025** deadline will lead to **penal charges**, which vary based on the percentage of the shortfall.
 
 

67:T
